nm.title: Nombor & Masa
nm.lead: Numbers, days, dates, money and the clock in Malaysian Malay. Open any time: before chapter 1 or alongside it. Practice only; your review schedule doesn't change.
nm.part.hari: Days of the week, yesterday, today, tomorrow
nm.chart.clock: Clock and parts of the day
nm.chart.zero: 0: kosong (everyday, and in phone numbers) or sifar (formal).
nm.chart.se: se- means one: sepuluh 10, sebelas 11, seratus 100, seribu 1,000, sejuta 1,000,000. Not satu ratus.
nm.chart.man: Malay counts in thousands: 10,000 = sepuluh ribu, 100,000 = seratus ribu.
nm.chart.build: Build a number from blocks, biggest first:
nm.chart.pukul: pukul is the clock time (pukul tiga = 3 o'clock); jam counts hours (dua jam = 2 hours).
nm.parts_note: The times are a guide: people's habits differ near the edges.
nm.drag: Drag the hands (the long hand near the edge), or spin.
nm.today_pick: Tap a day to make it today.
nm.q.relative: What do you call the ❓ day?
nm.no_voice: No Malay voice on this device: text only.
nm.hook.nombor.1: Same order as Japanese: dua ratus is two hundred, like 二百; tiga ribu is like 三千. But Malay has no 万: 10,000 is sepuluh ribu, 'ten thousand'.
nm.hook.nombor.2: belas is the teens, puluh the tens: empat belas = 14, empat puluh = 40. belas adds ten, puluh multiplies by ten.
nm.hook.hari.1: Count the week from Ahad (Sunday): Isnin is the 2nd day, Selasa the 3rd, Rabu the 4th, Khamis the 5th; then Jumaat and Sabtu.
nm.hook.hari.2: semalam has malam (night) inside: 'one night ago' is yesterday. esok is tomorrow, lusa the day after (あさって).
nm.hook.bulan.1: The months are the English names, Malaysian style: Mac, Jun, Julai, Ogos, Disember. Hear 'Aug' in Ogos.
nm.hook.bulan.2: A date goes day, month, year (the reverse of Japanese). The year is an ordinary big number: 2026 = dua ribu dua puluh enam.
nm.hook.pecahan.1: setengah is 半: pukul tiga setengah is 3時半, the same order as Japanese. suku is a quarter, tiga suku three quarters.
nm.hook.pecahan.2: Hear ratus (100) inside peratus: per hundred. perpuluhan is the decimal point: dua perpuluhan lima = 2.5.
nm.hook.wang.1: Ringgit first, then sen, like 円 with a second unit: RM12.50 = dua belas ringgit lima puluh sen.
nm.hook.wang.2: Watch RM4.50 against RM4.05: lima puluh sen is 50 sen, lima sen is 5 sen. In speech you will also hear empat ringgit setengah.
nm.hook.masa.1: The clock time is pukul (〜時); jam counts hours (〜時間): pukul dua = 2 o'clock, dua jam = 2 hours.
nm.hook.masa.2: Instead of am and pm, add the part of the day: pagi, tengah hari, petang (while it is light), malam (after dark).
